FacTweet extracts emotion, sentiment, morality, style and word-embedding features from tweets.
Emotion features form a vector from word occurrences across 15 emotion types, using the NRC and SentiSense lexicons. SentiSense categories not present in NRC are used.
Sentiment features use EffectWordNet, SenticNet, NRC and the subj lexicon, each with positive and negative classes.
Morality features label words using ten categories: care, harm, fairness, cheating, loyalty, betrayal, authority, subversion, sanctity and degradation.
Style features include counts of question marks, exclamation marks, consecutive characters and letters, links, hashtags and user mentions, as well as uppercase ratio and tweet length. These are examples rather than an exhaustive list.
Word embeddings are extracted using the pretrained Glove840B−300d model and averaged to obtain the tweet representation.

Annotation discrepancies arise from subjective judgment, with a greater impact on complex tasks such as image-based or multimodal detection than on text-only detection.
Multimodal hate publications use substantial background knowledge, making visual–textual relationships complex, diverse and difficult for a neural network to learn.
Although the collected dataset contains 150K tweets, its multimodal hate subset is still too small to learn the complex relationships needed to identify multimodal hate.

AMD’s 2022 net revenue rose 44% to $23.6 billion from $16.4 billion in 2021. Growth in Data Center, Gaming and Embedded was partially offset by a decline in Client revenue.
Data Center revenue increased 64% to $6 billion, primarily due to higher EPYC server processor sales.
Gaming revenue increased 21% to $6.8 billion, driven by higher semi-custom sales from demand for gaming console SoCs. Lower gaming graphics sales partially offset the increase, as shipments fell amid soft consumer demand and weakened macroeconomic conditions in the second half of 2022.
Embedded revenue increased significantly to $4.6 billion, primarily due to the inclusion of Xilinx embedded product revenue following the February 2022 acquisition.
Client revenue decreased 10% to $6.2 billion, primarily because unit shipments fell 24%, partially offset by a 19% increase in average selling price. Shipments fell amid challenging PC market conditions and supply-chain inventory corrections in the second half of 2022; the price increase primarily reflected a richer mix of Ryzen mobile processor sales.

Ulta Beauty reported fourth-quarter fiscal 2022 net sales of $3.2 billion, up 18.2%, and net income of $340.8 million, up 17.8% from a year earlier.
The thirteen-week quarter ended January 28, 2023. Sales growth was attributed primarily to the beauty category’s continued resilience, retail price increases, and new brands and product innovation.
Comparable sales rose 15.6%, driven by a 13.6% increase in transactions and a 1.8% increase in average ticket.
Gross profit rose 18.0% to $1.2 billion; its 37.6% share of net sales was flat, as favorable factors were offset by higher inventory shrink.
SG&A expenses rose 17.3% to $762.7 million but fell to 23.6% of net sales from 23.8%.
Operating income rose 19.2% to $447.6 million, or 13.9% of net sales. Diluted earnings per share rose 23.5% to $6.68, including a $0.02 benefit from income tax accounting for stock-based compensation.
At quarter-end, cash and cash equivalents were $737.9 million and net merchandise inventories were $1.6 billion, up from $1.5 billion a year earlier.
During the quarter, Ulta opened 12 stores, relocated one and remodeled 12; it ended the quarter with 1,355 stores.
Ulta repurchased 722,457 shares for $328.1 million during the quarter. As of January 28, 2023, $1.1 billion remained available under its $2.0 billion repurchase program.
